fields.features_heading: What Emergent Puts in a Fill in the Blank Quiz
fields.features_subheading: Describe the sentences, the answers you accept, and what a score should do. Emergent builds the quiz and the table behind it.
fields.feature_1:
Blanks drafted from your own text

Paste a passage or a list of terms, and Emergent drafts one sentence per blank with the answer you choose. A follow-up prompt swaps the word, moves the blank, or adds another.
fields.feature_2:
An answer list for every blank

Each blank holds the answers the app marks right, such as 7 and seven, or a word typed with or without its accent. Anything off that list scores as a miss or waits for you.
fields.feature_3:
Typed answers or a word bank

Takers type the missing word, or pick it from a word bank for younger classes. Either way they see one sentence per screen, which reads well on a phone held in one hand.
fields.feature_4:
Every answer saved by blank

Each submission saves as a row with the taker, the typed answer, and the blank it fills, in a database you own. Sort by blank and the one nobody gets right rises to the top.
fields.feature_5:
Pass marks and score emails

Set a pass mark or score bands, and the app emails the result to the taker, a manager, or both. Emergent puts no cap on responses, so a whole grade can take the same quiz.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and code to keep

Run the quiz on a custom domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and reuse it next term.

faq_heading: Fill in the Blank Quiz Questions, Answered

quiz.title: Fill in the Blank Quiz: 8 Solar System Facts
quiz.intro: Eight sentences about the planets and the Sun, each with one word missing. Pick the word that fills the blank; your score and the NASA source for each answer show at the end.

questions.text: The smallest planet in the solar system, and the nearest to the Sun, is ____.
questions.explanation: Mercury is both the smallest planet and the one closest to the Sun, only slightly larger than Earth's Moon.

source.quote: Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system and nearest to the Sun

questions.text: The hottest planet in the solar system is ____, even though it is not the closest to the Sun.
questions.explanation: Venus is second from the Sun, yet its thick atmosphere traps heat, so it runs hotter than Mercury.

source.quote: Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system

questions.text: Mars looks reddish because ____ in its rocks and dust is rusting.
questions.explanation: Iron in the Martian rocks, soil, and dust oxidizes, the same process that rusts a bike chain left outside.

source.quote: of iron in the rocks, regolith

questions.text: Mars has two small moons: Phobos and ____.
questions.explanation: Phobos and Deimos are small and potato-shaped, and NASA notes they may be captured asteroids.

source.quote: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos

questions.text: Jupiter is so large that if it were a hollow shell, about ____ Earths could fit inside.
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, big enough to hold about 1,000 Earths.

source.quote: if it were a hollow shell, 1,000 Earths could fit inside

questions.text: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a giant ____ that is bigger than Earth.
questions.explanation: The Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth that has raged for hundreds of years.

source.quote: Great Red Spot is a giant storm bigger than Earth

questions.text: Saturn's rings are made of billions of small chunks of ____ and rock.
questions.explanation: The ring pieces are chunks of ice and rock coated with dust, from tiny grains to pieces as big as a house.

source.quote: made of billions of small chunks of ice and rock

questions.text: The Sun is a 4.5 billion-year-old ____ star.
questions.explanation: The Sun is a yellow dwarf, a hot glowing ball of hydrogen and helium at the center of the solar system.

results.title: Ready for a Second Orbit
results.description: You filled 3 blanks or fewer. Read the NASA line under each answer, then take it again: the second pass is where the planet names start to stick.

results.title: Solid Solar System Basics
results.description: You filled 4 to 6 blanks. You know the planets by name; the details, like what Saturn's rings are made of, are what separate you from a perfect score.

results.title: Mission Ready
results.description: You filled 7 or 8 blanks. A teacher could build this same quiz with typed answers instead of a word bank, and you would still pass it.

plan.angle: Searchers for fill in the blank quiz want a quiz to take or a tool to make one, and the hard part of the format is grading typed answers. This page gives both: an 8-question solar system fill in the blank quiz to play on the page with a NASA source behind every answer, then four builds where the grading rule matters: a Spanish teacher whose blanks accept a word with or without its accent mark, an inn whose new hires need 9 of 10 blanks before a front desk shift, a biology teacher whose off-list answers wait in a review queue, and an adult reading center that places learners with a cloze-style passage.
tab_stories: Graciela Faraone's weekly Spanish vocabulary quiz at Kesterwood Middle School has 15 blanks that accept a word with or without its accent mark, and the results table ranks words by misses so the top 4 open Monday's lesson.

Hollins Wharf Inn gives each new front desk hire a 10-blank quiz on its check-in steps; 9 or 10 passes and emails the shift manager, anything lower sends the hire back to the module, and 11 of 14 hires passed on the first try this spring.

Ingrid Solvang's 31 biology students at Aldergate High fill 12 blanks on cell parts; typed answers not on her accepted list wait in a review queue, and of 372 answers, 19 landed there and she accepted 7.

Bexley Row Learning Center has each new adult learner fill 30 blanks in a short news story, one every seventh word, and score bands place the 48 September learners into 3 reading groups of 15, 20, and 13.
